metadata.summary: Arsenal's Kroenke family owners tend not to get involved in transfer dealings but when it came to Declan Rice, and the prospect of spending £100m on a player for the first time, they needed to be sure that it was a sensible investment.
metadata.content: Declan Rice: Arsenal's 'total player' and £105m bargain can unlock more levels after agreeing new contract | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Declan Rice: Arsenal's 'total player' and £105m bargain can unlock more levels after agreeing new contract Declan Rice has agreed a new long term-contract at Arsenal so can he continue to go from strength to strength? So, in the conference room at Arsenal's training ground, co-chair Josh Kroenke asked to be walked through the deal by Mikel Arteta, former sporting director Edu, then executive vice-chair Tim Lewis and now chief executive officer Richard Garlick. "My eyebrows raised because I didn't know if we were in that phase just yet to go after a player like that," Kroenke recalled. He wanted to know what he would bring and how Arteta would use him. He wanted reassurance that he could hit the ground running. Kroenke left the meeting in no doubt about the deal, either financially or in footballing terms. messages.text: Ratcliffe's Ineos Group settles £10m-plus claim with Ainslie's firm over yacht

metadata.summary: A company connected to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group said it has settled a High Court claim against a firm founded by Sir Ben Ainslie.
metadata.content: Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group settles £10m-plus claim with Sir Ben Ainslie's Athena Racing over alleged non-return of yacht | Sailing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group settles £10m-plus claim with Sir Ben Ainslie's Athena Racing over alleged non-return of yacht Ineos Racing sued Athena Racing earlier this year, alleging the latter breached a deal between the two companies by refusing to return multimillion-pound yacht; Sir Ben Ainslie's GB1 team is the challenger of record for the next America's Cup in Naples, Italy in 2027 Monday 16 November 2026 13:03, UK Image: A company connected to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group said it has settled a High Court claim against a firm founded by Sir Ben Ainslie A company connected to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group said it has settled a High Court claim against a firm founded by Sir Ben Ainslie. Ineos Racing sued Athena Racing earlier this year, alleging the latter breached a deal between the two companies by refusing to return the multimillion-pound yacht Ineos Britannia, which Ainslie captained at the 2024 America's Cup in a 7-2 defeat to Emirates Team New Zealand in Barcelona. Lawyers for Ineos said in court documents filed earlier this year that the claim was valued at more than £10 million. Sky Sports on WhatsApp: Breaking news, videos and analysis Not got Sky?
